description: Implement the shared :core domain: wire protocol (message types + length-prefixed framing + JSON serialization), the pairing module (short code / QR payload generation + shared-secret derivation), end-to-end encryption helpers (symmetric AEAD seal/open over an envelope, key derivation from the pairing secret via HKDF), and the device/transfer data models. This is the transport-independent heart used identically by the LAN path and the relay path, so remote operation and local operation share one protocol. All of this is pure JVM Kotlin and must be unit-tested in the sandbox.
steps: Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/model/ with @Serializable data classes: DeviceInfo (id, displayName, deviceType enum PHONE/TABLET/LAPTOP, publicKeyFingerprint), PairedDevice, and TransferKind enum (CLIPBOARD_TEXT, SCREENSHOT, FILE, PHOTO).

Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/protocol/Message.kt: a sealed hierarchy / @Serializable envelope `Envelope(fromDeviceId, toDeviceId, pairingId, kind, nonceB64, ciphertextB64)` plus inner payload types ClipboardPayload(text), FileMetaPayload(name, mimeType, sizeBytes, sha256), FileChunkPayload(index, totalChunks, dataB64). Use kotlinx.serialization JSON.

Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/protocol/Framing.kt: length-prefixed framing (4-byte big-endian length + UTF-8 JSON) with writeFrame(OutputStream, bytes) and readFrame(InputStream): ByteArray, guarding against oversized frames. This is used by the direct-socket LAN transport; the relay path sends the same JSON envelopes as WebSocket text frames.

Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/crypto/E2E.kt: wrap JVM javax.crypto AES-256-GCM. Provide deriveLinkKey(pairingSecret: ByteArray, context: String): SecretKey via HKDF-SHA256 (implement HKDF with javax.crypto.Mac HmacSHA256, no third-party dep), seal(key, plaintext): (nonce, ciphertext) with a random 12-byte nonce, and open(key, nonce, ciphertext): plaintext. Keep this Android-compatible (only javax.crypto APIs present on API 26+).

Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/pairing/Pairing.kt: generate a pairing secret (32 random bytes), encode a QR/short-code pairing payload (pairingId + initiator DeviceInfo + base64 secret) as compact JSON and a 8-char human-typable short code mapping to it (document that the short code indexes an in-memory/relay-held pending pairing, while QR carries the full secret). Provide parsePairingPayload().

Create core/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/core/protocol/EnvelopeCodec.kt: high-level sealEnvelope(linkKey, from, to, pairingId, kind, plaintextJson) -> Envelope and openEnvelope(linkKey, Envelope) -> plaintext bytes, tying crypto + models together so :app and :relay-tests use one API.

Create core/src/test/kotlin/com/linkup/core/ tests: (a) FramingTest round-trips frames incl. empty and large payloads and rejects oversized; (b) E2ETest verifies seal/open round-trip, that a wrong key fails to open (AEADBadTagException), and HKDF determinism + different context => different key; (c) EnvelopeCodecTest round-trips a ClipboardPayload through seal/open; (d) PairingTest round-trips a pairing payload and asserts the secret survives encode/parse.
Delete or fold the FEAT-001 placeholder test once real tests exist (keep :core:test meaningful).
acceptance_criteria: `./gradlew :core:test` passes all new tests in the sandbox.
E2ETest proves that an Envelope sealed with one link key cannot be opened with a different key (tamper/isolation guarantee).
The same Envelope JSON produced by EnvelopeCodec is byte-identical whether destined for LAN framing or relay WebSocket (one protocol for both transports).
No Android imports anywhere under core/ (only kotlin, kotlinx, java.*, javax.crypto).
verification: Run `grep -rn "android" core/src/main` and confirm no Android imports leaked into :core.
findings: REVIEW FIX (2026-10-02, review 071415): Addressed the concurrent-transfer corruption (review issue #3) and the one-directional pairing (review issue #2) at the :core protocol layer. (a) Added `transferId: String` to BOTH FileMetaPayload and FileChunkPayload so inbound chunks are attributed by transfer, not by 'first in-flight transfer for this pairing'. (b) Added a pure-JVM, unit-tested `protocol/FileReassembler.kt` that holds all chunk matching/buffering/sha256 verification keyed on `pairingId:transferId`; the Android FileShare now delegates to it. New `FileReassemblerTest` (6 tests) includes a REGRESSION test (`two concurrent transfers in one pairing do not corrupt each other`) that fails without the transferId keying. (c) Added `TransferKind.PAIRING_HELLO` and `PairingHelloPayload(device)` so the QR scanner can send its DeviceInfo back to the initiator (bidirectional pairing); covered by a new EnvelopeCodecTest case. Payload disambiguation still holds (meta vs chunk have disjoint required fields). All green: `./gradlew :core:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, core now 28 tests (EnvelopeCodec 4, FileReassembler 6, E2E 6, Framing 7, Pairing 5). No Android imports in :core. --- ORIGINAL: Implemented entirely in :core (pure Kotlin/JVM), fully verified in sandbox. `./gradlew :core:test` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL with 21 passing tests (FramingTest 6, E2ETest 7, EnvelopeCodecTest 3, PairingTest 5). `grep -rn android core/src/main` -> no matches. Files: model/Models.kt (DeviceInfo, PairedDevice, DeviceType, TransferKind), protocol/Message.kt (@Serializable Envelope + ClipboardPayload/FileMetaPayload/FileChunkPayload, shared WireJson config), protocol/Framing.kt (4-byte big-endian length prefix, MAX_FRAME_SIZE=16MiB guard on both read and write, EOFException on truncation), crypto/E2E.kt (AES-256-GCM seal/open with random 12-byte nonce, HKDF-SHA256 via javax.crypto.Mac HmacSHA256, deriveLinkKey), pairing/Pairing.kt (32-byte secret, PairingPayload compact JSON, 8-char Crockford-base32 short code documented as a handle to a pending pairing while QR carries the full secret, parsePairingPayload), protocol/EnvelopeCodec.kt (sealEnvelope/openEnvelope). Wrong-key open raises AEADBadTagException (verified in E2ETest + EnvelopeCodecTest). One JSON serialization is reused byte-identically for LAN framing and relay WebSocket (EnvelopeCodecTest). Only javax.crypto / java.* / kotlinx used -> Android API 26+ compatible. Deviations: removed FEAT-001 placeholder LinkupTest.kt (committed in scaffold, now git-removed); Linkup.kt metadata object kept (harmless, no test depends on it now). Added `.kotlin/` (Kotlin build daemon dir) to .gitignore. Reused existing catalog deps; no new catalog entries needed. gradle.properties JDK 17 setting left untouched.
